name: Abiasaf
title: Levitical clan leader from the line of Korah
summary: Abiasaph was a Levite belonging to the family of Korah, listed as one of Korah's sons in Exod 6:24. Although his father Korah led a rebellion against Moses and Aaron in the wilderness and was struck by God's judgment, Korah's sons were spared (Num 26:11) – a striking example that God's punishment does not automatically pass down through generations. Abiasaph became an important ancestor within the Levitical service. His descendants received prominent roles in Israel's worship life: the Korahites served as gatekeepers at the sanctuary (1 Chr 9:19) and as singers in the temple. Through his lineage descended the singer Heman, whom King David appointed as leader of praise (1 Chr 6:33–38). The name form Ebiasaph in 1 Chr 6:22–23 is considered by most scholars to be a variant of Abiasaph, and the two are usually identified as the same person.

keyEvents.title: Mentioned in the genealogy of Korah
keyEvents.description: Abiasaf is listed as one of the sons of Korah in the Levitical genealogy, confirming his place in the tribe of Levi.

keyEvents.title: Korah's Sons Spared During the Rebellion
keyEvents.description: Abiasaf's father, Korah, led a rebellion against Moses and Aaron in the wilderness and was struck by God's judgment. According to Numbers 16, the rebels perished—Dathan and Abiram were swallowed by the earth, while Korah and the 250 men with their incense burners were consumed by fire from the Lord. However, Korah's sons, including Abiasaf, were spared from punishment.

keyEvents.title: Genealogy in First Chronicles
keyEvents.description: Abiasaf (here called Ebiasaph) is mentioned in the detailed Levitical genealogy in 1 Chronicles, showing his connection to the Levitical service and his place in the family tree.

keyEvents.title: The Role of the Korahites as Gatekeepers
keyEvents.description: The descendants of Korah, including Abiasaf's line, were given the task of serving as gatekeepers at the Lord's dwelling, a duty that tradition traces back to the wilderness period.

keyEvents.title: Connection to the Singer Heman
keyEvents.description: Through Abiasaf's lineage descended the singer Heman, who was appointed by David to lead worship in the temple.

versions.summary: Abiasaf was a Levite from Korah's family, son of Korah, and one of the ancestors of the Levitical temple gatekeepers and singers. Despite his father Korah rebelling against Moses, Korah's sons were spared and continued to serve in God's house. Abiasaf is an important link in the Levitical genealogy that led to the prophet Samuel and the singer Heman.
versions.title: Levitical Clan Leader from Korah's Line
versions.reason: [minor] The title has a small grammatical error: 'klanoverhodet' should be 'klanoverhode' (indefinite form) to fit the context, as the definite form after 'levittisk' is unusual.; [major] Abiasaf is not referred to as a 'priest' in the Bible. He is mentioned as part of the Levitical lineage, but there is no text assigning him priestly service. The role of 'leader' is also weakly documented. More precise roles would be 'Levite' and 'ancestor', given his function in the genealogies.; [major] According to Exodus 6:24, Korah's sons were Assir, Elkanah, and Abiasaf. This matches the layout, but 'Elkanah' should be verified as the correct ID. In 1 Chronicles 6:22–23, the genealogical order is slightly different (Assir, Elkanah, Ebjasaf/Abiasaf), which may suggest that Elkanah here was a brother, though some scholars argue it represents a linear lineage rather than brothers. The data are acceptable based on Exodus 6:24, but this should be noted.; [critical] The reference is given as Exodus 6:24 (bookId: 2), which is the correct book (Exodus = bookId 2). This aligns with Abiasaf being mentioned among Korah's sons in Exodus 6:24.; [minor] 1 Chronicles 6:22–23 and 6:37 mention Abiasaf/Ebjasaf in the lineage. The verses may vary between different translations (some have different verse numbering in 1 Chronicles 6). Verse numbers should be verified against multiple translations, as some place Ebjasaf in verse 37 while others place him in verse 23.; [minor] The summary states that Abiasaf is a 'son of Korah', but it should clarify that this is based on Exodus 6:24, whereas 1 Chronicles 6 may indicate a linear lineage where Abiasaf/Ebjasaf is a descendant several generations later. Otherwise, the summary is well formulated.; [major] Footnotes are missing. A profile like this should include footnotes about the meaning of the name (Abiasaf = 'my father has gathered'), the relationship between the name forms Abiasaf and Ebjasaf, and the theological significance that Korah's sons were spared.; [minor] The dating 'c. 1400 BC' assumes an early date for the Exodus. This is acceptable, but it should be noted that the dating of the Exodus is debated (c. 1446 or c. 1270 BC).

versions.reason: [major] The final footnote claims that Abiasaf/Ebjasaf stands in the direct lineage leading to the prophet Samuel. According to 1 Chr 6:33-38, Heman's lineage is through the Kohathite clan, but Samuel belongs to another branch of the Levites (through Elkanah from a different line, cf. 1 Sam 1:1). It is disputed and problematic to link Samuel directly to Abiasaf. This claim should be removed or nuanced.; [minor] The verse numbers in 1 Chr 6 vary between the Hebrew text and translations. In many translations, Ebjasaf is mentioned in verses 22-23 and the lineage in verse 37, but some number the verses differently (e.g., 6:8, 22, 37 in Hebrew vs. 6:22, 23, 37 in translations). It should be checked that the references match the numbering used.; [minor] The summary is good, but the sentence "The name form Ebjasaf in 1 Chronicles is considered a variant of Abiasaf" could usefully specify that this applies to 1 Chr 6:22-23 to provide a more concrete reference.; [minor] The role "clan leader" appearing in the title is not reflected in the roles array. Consider adding "clan leader" as a role, or alternatively adjust the title.

footnotes.text: The name Abiasaf (Hebrew: אֲבִיאָסָף, 'Aviasaf') means 'my father has gathered' or 'my father has added.' The name expresses gratitude to God who has 'gathered' or 'added' a child to the family.

In 1 Chronicles 6:22, the name form Ebiasaph (אֶבְיָסָף) is used, which is considered a variant of Abiasaf. Most scholars regard this as the same person, with the difference arising from various traditions in the transmission of the name.

According to Numbers 26:11, Korah's sons did not die when their father was punished for rebelling against Moses. This is theologically significant: God's judgment on Korah did not automatically extend to his descendants. The principle of individual responsibility—that children should not be punished for their parents' sins—is an important theological theme in the Old Testament (cf. Deuteronomy 24:16; Ezekiel 18:20).

The Korahites are associated with a number of psalms in the Book of Psalms (Ps 42, 44–49, 84–85, 87–88), which testifies to the rich musical tradition among Korah's descendants. The fact that the lineage of the rebel Korah was transformed into leaders of praise is a powerful image of grace and restoration.

In 1 Chron 9:19, the Korahites are described as gatekeepers at the entrance of the tabernacle. Archaeological findings from the Arad sanctuary in the Negev desert have revealed traces of organized cultic services with specialized roles, providing material context for the biblical descriptions of Levitical duties.

The genealogies in 1 Chron 6 place Abiasaf/Ebjasaf in the direct lineage leading to the singer Heman (1 Chron 6:33–38). Heman was one of three singers David appointed to lead worship, along with Asaph and Ethan/Jeduthun, underscoring the great significance of Korah's descendants in Israel's cultic life.

The rabbinic tradition (Talmud, Sanhedrin 110a) discusses how Korah's sons were spared, and some rabbis explain that they repented at the last moment. Midrash Tehillim links them to the psalms bearing their names and sees their survival as a testimony to teshuva (repentance).
